name: spec-ship
description: Ship a built spec. Runs the project's tests and stops on failure, refuses to ship behavior without the owner's recorded go, has a fresh reviewer compare the diff with the spec and the plan, removes code no claim covers, copies the spec's claims into behavior/ without rewording, updates the architecture files the plan lists, sets the status to shipped, and prepares the pull request with its title, template, review findings and outcome, asking whether to create it or show it. Never merges. Use when a user asks to ship, finish, wrap up or open the pull request for a spec, or runs spec-ship.

# spec-ship

Code and docs land together, reviewed by someone who didn't write them, and the owner's go is on record.

## Process

1. Load docs-conventions. `references/behavior.md`, `references/architecture.md`, `references/index.md` and `references/spec.md` apply.
2. Find the active spec from the branch. Read `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`. If a task is unticked, say which and stop.
3. Gate on the go. A feature, or a fix with claims under What changes, needs the `approved` line. Without it, say "The owner of <domain>/<capability> hasn't said go" and stop. A fix with "No behavior change" needs none.
4. Run the project's test command from `architecture/stack.md`. If anything fails, report it and stop. No docs change on a red run.
5. Fresh review. Ask a reviewer that did not write the code, a sub-agent with a fresh context or, without one, a separate read-only session of the agent started from the shell with the review prompt, to compare the branch's diff against main with the claims in `spec.md` and the Files list in `plan.md`, and to report: claims with no test carrying their reference, behavior in the diff that no claim covers, files changed outside the plan, and anything in the diff that contradicts a claim. Keep the findings for the pull request; code files outside the plan become its Unrelated changes. The docs the flow itself writes, the spec folder, `behavior/`, `architecture/`, `decisions/`, `glossary.md`, `index.md`, the block in `AGENTS.md` and the `CLAUDE.md` import, are never unrelated.
6. Uncovered code. For each finding of behavior no claim covers, remove the code and the tests that exercise it, without asking: the spec is the contract. A test-only helper that nothing outside the tests calls is not behavior and stays. Run the tests again and stop on red. The Review section names each removal. An owner who wants the code back adds a claim for it, which is a change to `spec.md` with a new go, and only when the owner says so in the session does the claim get written instead of the removal.
7. Update `behavior/`. For each `### Add · <domain>/<capability>`, create or extend `behavior/<domain>/<capability>.md` from its template with the claims copied word for word. For each Change, replace the claim with that ID in place. For each Remove, delete the claim. Reword nothing.
8. Update architecture. For each line under Architecture to update at ship in `plan.md`, update that area file from the named reference file, creating it from its template when it doesn't exist. Leave the reference file as it is. Add a domain row to `index.md` only when one is still missing.
9. Set `status: shipped` in `spec.md`. The status becomes true on the main branch exactly when the pull request merges.
10. Outcome. Count the Session lines in `tasks.md`. Ask the user which of those sessions needed re-explaining, one question. Compare `request:` with the shipped claims and write one line on what grilling added, changed or kept out.
11. The pull request. Title: `type(scope): objective`, type being the kind written out, `feature` or `fix`, never the short `feat`, and `refactor` for a fix with no behavior change; scope the `issue:` key or else the slug; objective the spec's title. Description: if the repo has `.github/pull_request_template.md` or `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`, fill its sections and add Review and Outcome at the end. Otherwise use the layout below. Propose Release impact from the kind and the claims, MINOR for a feature, PATCH for a fix with claims, "No release impact" for a fix without, MAJOR when a claim is removed, and ask the user to confirm it in the same question as the sessions. Then ask whether to create the pull request with `gh` or to show the title and description to paste. Without `gh`, show them. Never merge.

```
## Links
- **<Tracker>:** <KEY>: <spec title>, linked as <issue-tracker><KEY>   or   None.
- **Spec:** docs/specs/<id>/spec.md

## Description
<the Why in one or two lines, then one line per claim added, changed or removed>

## Unrelated changes
<files changed outside plan.md, one per line>   or   None.

## Release impact
**Release impact:** <No release impact | PATCH | MINOR | MAJOR>

## Review
<the fresh reviewer's findings, each uncovered behavior marked removed or claimed, or "No findings.">

## Outcome
Sessions: <n>, re-explained: <n>. <what grilling added, changed or kept out>.
```

## Verification

- The tests passed on the branch before any docs changed.
- Every claim under Add, Change and Remove is reflected in `behavior/`, word for word.
- Every area file named in `plan.md` was updated, and no reference file changed.
- `spec.md` says `status: shipped` and carries the `approved` line when claims changed.
- The pull request text has every section filled and no placeholder.

## Rationalizations and red flags

| Excuse | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| "One flaky test, I'll ship anyway." | Red run, no ship. Fix or stop. |
| "I reviewed my own diff carefully." | The reviewer is a fresh context that didn't write the code. A review done in this session is never written up as fresh: without a sub-agent, start a separate session from the shell, or, without a shell, stop and hand the user the review prompt. |
| "I'll tidy the claim wording while copying." | Claims are copied word for word. Rewording is a Change in a later spec. |
| "No owner around, but the fix is small." | A fix with claims needs the go. Show the text to paste and stop. |
| "I'll merge it, the user asked to ship." | spec-ship never merges. |
| "The review found an extra helper, but it is harmless, I'll leave it." | Code no claim covers is removed before the docs change. Harmless today is precedent tomorrow. |
| "I'll ask whether they want to keep it before removing." | Removal is the default and needs no question. The owner brings code back with a claim and a go. |

## Fallbacks

- No sub-agents: start a separate read-only session of the agent from the shell with the review prompt, wait for it, and take its findings. Codex: `codex exec --sandbox read-only "<the review prompt>" < /dev/null`, which the sandbox blocks, so ask to run it with escalated permissions. Without a shell either: stop before any docs change, give the user the review prompt to run in a fresh session, and wait for the findings. Either way, say in the pull request that the review ran in a separate session.
- No shell in this session: ask the user to run the test command and report the result, and ship only on a reported green run.
- No `gh`: show the title and the description to paste.
- No question tool: ask the two questions in plain text and wait.

It says which file holds what, what each never contains, where misplaced content goes, and how a claim is written.

# Docs conventions

Project memory lives under the docs path the project-memory block in AGENTS.md names, `docs/` unless the block says otherwise. Every file has one job. Content that matches a file's "never contains" column goes to the file the charter names for it.

## Process

1. Find the file's row in the charter. Read its reference under `references/` for the sections and their rules, and start from its template under `assets/`.
2. Write only what the file's job covers. Move anything else to the file the row names.
3. Remove every `<!-- -->` guidance comment. Delete an optional section that would be empty. Never write "None", "TBD" or a line saying the content is still to come: while an answer is still being settled, a required section keeps its heading and nothing under it, and the file is not done until every section left has content. Keep heading names and their order exactly as the template has them.
4. Keep the frontmatter keys the template has, with no comments in the frontmatter. A quoted slot such as `id: "{{slug}}"` is filled without the quotes, unless the value needs them to stay valid YAML.
5. Write claims in the claim format below, 3 to 7 per capability.

## The charter

| File | Job | Contains | Never contains, and where that goes | Template | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `index.md` | map of the product and its docs | what it is, the domains with their owners, where things are | details of any domain: `behavior/` | `assets/index.md` | `references/index.md` |
| `glossary.md` | shared words | term, meaning, name in code, words to avoid | rules or behavior: `behavior/` | none, one line per term | `references/glossary.md` |
| `behavior/<domain>/<capability>.md` | what the product does now | claims with IDs, one example each | how it's built: `architecture/`; history: git; plans: `specs/` | `assets/behavior-capability.md` | `references/behavior.md` |
| `architecture/<area>.md` | how it's built now | one area per file, created when it first has content | behavior: `behavior/`; history: git; plans: `specs/` | `assets/architecture/` | `references/architecture.md` |
| `decisions/<date>-<slug>.md` | why a lasting choice was made | context, options, decision, consequences | step-by-step detail: `plan.md` or `reference/` | `assets/decision.md` | `references/decision.md` |
| `specs/<id>/spec.md` | why this change, and exactly what changes | why, claims under Add, Change and Remove, not doing, open questions | how it's built: `plan.md`; progress: `tasks.md` | `assets/spec.md` | `references/spec.md` |
| `specs/<id>/plan.md` | how this change is built | approach, files to touch, architecture to update at ship, risks | the why: `spec.md`; progress: `tasks.md` | `assets/plan.md` | `references/plan.md` |
| `specs/<id>/tasks.md` | where the work stands | session lines, tasks with the claims that prove them, short notes | design discussion: `plan.md` or `decisions/` | `assets/tasks.md` | `references/tasks.md` |
| `specs/<id>/reference/*` | working material for this spec | anything the spec needs, opening with `Purpose: ...` | the why, the plan, progress: the three files above | none | `references/reference.md` |
| AGENTS.md block | the workflow and where memory lives | the managed block between the markers | project knowledge: `docs/` | `assets/agents-block.md` | `references/agents-block.md` |

## The claim format

```
- <Actor> <does or sees something observable, present tense> {#claim-id}
  e.g. <a concrete situation> -> <the observable result>
```

One testable sentence per claim, then one concrete example. IDs are kebab-case and unique within their capability. The full reference is `domain/capability#claim-id`; tests carry it in their names, and tasks use it whenever the bare ID is not unique in the spec. Observable behavior only: "keeps one entry", never "uses a unique index". A claim in `spec.md` reads exactly as it will in `behavior/`, so shipping copies it without rewording.

## Versions

`index.md` carries `docs-format`. A template change applies to new files only. Shipped specs and existing files are never rewritten to a newer format.

## Writing

Every file the pack writes is in plain words. No opener that announces what follows, no hedge or intensifier, no jargon, no em dash, no rhetorical setup. Active voice, one idea per sentence, a specific over an adjective: a number, a name, an example. The templates' limits are the length; a file that needs more words than its template allows needs a shorter idea.

## Verification

- The file has the template's frontmatter keys and headings, in the template's order, and no `<!-- -->` comment anywhere.
- No section is empty, and "None" and "TBD" appear nowhere.
- Every claim has an ID and an `e.g.` line, and a capability has 3 to 7 of them.
- Nothing in the file matches its "never contains" column.

# Webshop

## What it is
This is a small webshop where customers buy outdoor gear. Customers send items back when they do not fit, and support handles returns and refunds.

## Domains
| Domain | Covers | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| returns | Customer returns and refunds | Sanne |
| wishlist | Saving, viewing and removing saved products | Sanne |

## Behavior
See [behavior/](behavior/): one folder per domain, one file per capability, each a short list of claims with IDs.

## Architecture
See [architecture/](architecture/): one file per area, `stack.md` first.
# Webshop

<!-- project-memory:start · managed by docs-init; edit outside these markers -->
## Project memory
- Start every task at docs/index.md, or at the active spec's tasks.md on a spec
  branch, and load only what they link to. Load glossary.md when naming things and
  decisions/ before changing a lasting choice.
- Answer what the product does from docs/behavior/; open the code only to change it.
- Every code change belongs to a spec in docs/specs/. None yet: start one (spec-start).
- One branch per spec, named after its slug. The active spec is the one matching the current branch.
- Every session adds its line to tasks.md. If something changes mid-way, update spec.md
  or plan.md, then recheck every task.
- Write specs, plans, tasks, glossary terms and decisions into docs/,
  never into SPEC.md, tasks/, CONTEXT.md or docs/superpowers/.
- Before opening a pull request, ship the spec (spec-ship); the PR title starts with the slug.
<!-- project-memory:end -->

Purpose: rules for `behavior/<domain>/<capability>.md`. Template: `assets/behavior-capability.md`.

Frontmatter: `capability`, as `<domain>/<capability>`.

Title: the capability as a verb phrase, such as "Save an item to the wishlist".

Body: the claims, in the claim format, 3 to 7 of them, and nothing else. Observable behavior only. Owners live in index.md, history in git, code locations in architecture/boundaries.md, and how it's built in architecture/.

Written by docs-map when a domain is mapped and by spec-ship when a spec ships, which copies the spec's claims without rewording and applies each Add, Change and Remove. Never edited by hand during a spec; a change to a claim is a Change in the spec that ships it.
Purpose: rules for `architecture/<area>.md`. Templates: `assets/architecture/<area>.md`.

Frontmatter: `area`, the area name. A title, then the area's own table or list. Current state only: no history, no plans. The why links to decision records.

Area files are created the first time they have content, never empty. `stack.md` exists from init, with the commands spec-build and spec-ship run. The folder listing is its own index.

| Area | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `stack` | languages and frameworks, and the commands to install, run, test, lint and build |
| `conventions` | only the rules agents get wrong without being told: naming, error handling, test style |
| `boundaries` | modules: name, path, domain, what each may depend on |
| `data-model` | entities: name, key fields, relations |
| `contracts` | APIs and events: name, kind, input, output, consumers |
| `integrations` | external services: purpose, direction, auth, what the product does when it fails |
| `config` | settings and flags: name, purpose, default, where it's set; never real secret values |
| `invariants` | non-negotiable rules every spec must keep: ID, rule, why |

Written by docs-map for what a domain needs, and by spec-ship for the files plan.md lists under Architecture to update at ship.
Purpose: rules for `index.md`. Template: `assets/index.md`.

Frontmatter: `product`, the product name; `docs-format`, the template version the project uses; `issue-tracker`, optional, the address a ticket key is appended to, such as `https://example.atlassian.net/browse/`, deleted when the team has none.

What it is: who uses the product and for what, in 2 to 4 sentences, in the user's words. Not a feature list.

Domains: a table with at least one row: domain, what it covers, owner. docs-init asks for the first row. spec-start and docs-map add a row the moment a new domain is named, before any go is asked. The owner is who says go for that domain; on a solo project, that is the user. A domain's behavior lives at `behavior/<domain>/`, so there is no link column.

Behavior: one line pointing at `behavior/`, so an agent that loads only what index.md links to finds the claims. Architecture: one line pointing at `architecture/`.

Nothing else: details of any domain belong in behavior/.
Purpose: section rules for `specs/<id>/spec.md`. Template: `assets/spec.md`.

Frontmatter: `id` as YYYY-MM-DD-slug; `kind`, feature or fix; `status`, draft, building or shipped; `summary`, one user-facing line reused in release notes; `request`, the sentence, issue or commits it started from; `issue`, optional, delete the line when there is none. The owner's go is `approved: {by: <owner>, via: <in session, a message link, or a PR>}`, added only when the user reports it, never inferred; git dates it. After a change to Why or What changes, remove the line; the owner's new go writes it back. The go is never a status.

Why: required. The problem, who has it, and what it costs to leave it, in 2 to 5 lines. No solution.

What changes: required. Claims under `### Add · <domain>/<capability>`, `### Change · ...` and `### Remove · ...`, only the headings that apply, one per capability. A Change claim carries a `was:` line with the current text on main. A Remove claim carries a `reason:` line. A fix that changes no behavior writes "No behavior change." and nothing else here. Claims read exactly as they will in behavior/.

Not doing: required for a feature, optional for a fix. What is deliberately out, so scope can't creep silently. Not future ideas with no decision behind them.

Open questions: while drafting, only questions the owner can answer. Delete the section when empty; the owner can't say go before that. Questions the agent can answer from the code never go here.

A spec past about 80 lines is two specs.
Purpose: rules for `specs/<id>/tasks.md`. Template: `assets/tasks.md`.

Frontmatter: `spec`, the spec id.

Above the tasks, one line per session, newest last, facts only and never a verdict: `Session YYYY-MM-DD: resumed at Tn; first message: "<gist of the user's first message>".` After a change mid-way, one more line: `Rechecked YYYY-MM-DD after: <the change>. T2 redo, T4 new, T5 dropped.`

Tasks: `- [ ] T<n> <imperative task> -> <claim IDs, or "check: <command or observable result>">`. Each task fits in one session. Tasks cover the build only; shipping is spec-ship's and is never a task. Numbers are never reused. A claim is written as `capability#id` when its bare ID is not unique in the spec. A task is ticked only when the claims it names are proven.

Under a task, at most two lines: `- note: <blocked, tried, why>` or `- redo: <what changed>`, the task unticked again. While a task is open, one more line may sit under it, `- handoff: done: <what exists>; red: <what fails or is unfinished>; next: <the first step>`, written when a session stops before the tick and removed at the tick. A dropped task is removed and named in the recheck line. Anything lasting in a note moves to plan.md or a decision record.

Nothing else: no design discussion, no why.

# Save items to a wishlist

## Why

Customers can lose track of products they are interested in but are not ready to buy.
Finding those products again takes effort, and customers may never return to complete the purchase.
Success means customers return to saved products and those saved products turn into orders.

## What changes

### Add · wishlist/save-items

- Callers can save any catalogue product to a wishlist using a supplied `customerId` string. {#save-item}
  e.g. A caller saves a headlamp for customer-1 -> the headlamp is included in customer-1's wishlist.

- Callers use one wishlist per `customerId` without signing in or creating a customer record. {#customer-id-wishlist}
  e.g. A caller saves a headlamp and then a tent for customer-1 without signing in -> both products belong to the same customer-1 wishlist.

- Callers save products without quantities. {#product-only-items}
  e.g. A caller saves a headlamp -> the saved item represents the headlamp product without a quantity.

- Callers receive an error when saving a product ID that is absent from the catalogue. {#reject-unknown-product}
  e.g. A caller tries to save a product ID that the catalogue does not contain -> saving fails with an error.

- Callers leave the wishlist unchanged when saving a product already on it, retaining one entry and its original save moment. {#preserve-first-save}
  e.g. A caller saves a headlamp at 10:00, a tent at 10:05 and the headlamp again at 10:10 -> the headlamp remains one entry saved at 10:00, behind the tent.

### Add · wishlist/view-items

- Callers see only the saved products associated with the `customerId` they supply. {#isolate-wishlists}
  e.g. Customer-1 has saved a headlamp and customer-2 has saved a tent -> viewing customer-2's wishlist shows only the tent.

- Callers see each saved product with its name and the price the catalogue currently holds. {#current-product-details}
  e.g. A headlamp was saved when its catalogue price was 3000 cents, and the catalogue now lists it at 3500 cents -> the wishlist shows the headlamp's name and 3500 cents.

- Callers see saved products ordered from most recently saved to least recently saved. {#newest-first}
  e.g. A headlamp was saved at 10:00 and a tent at 10:05 -> viewing the wishlist returns the tent before the headlamp.

- Callers receive an empty list when the supplied `customerId` has no saved products. {#empty-list}
  e.g. Customer-1 has no saved products -> viewing customer-1's wishlist returns an empty list without an error.

### Add · wishlist/remove-items

- Callers can remove a saved product from the wishlist identified by the supplied `customerId`. {#remove-item}
  e.g. A caller removes the headlamp saved for customer-1 -> the headlamp no longer appears in customer-1's wishlist.

- Callers receive an error when removing a product that is not on the addressed wishlist. {#reject-unsaved-product}
  e.g. Customer-1 has saved only a tent, and a caller tries to remove a headlamp from that wishlist -> removal fails with an error.

- Callers leave other customers' wishlists unchanged when removing a saved product. {#isolate-removal}
  e.g. Customer-1 and customer-2 both saved a headlamp, and a caller removes it for customer-1 -> customer-2's wishlist still contains the headlamp.

## Not doing

- Sign-in or a new customer entity.
- Buying from the wishlist; that belongs to a separate spec.
- Sharing wishlists, named lists or multiple lists per customer.
- Price or stock alerts.
- Quantities or price snapshots on saved items.
- Stock handling or behavior for products becoming unavailable or disappearing from the catalogue; the catalogue is currently fixed.

spec: 2026-10-13-customer-wishlist
---
## Approach

Implement `src/wishlist.ts` with a module-local Map keyed by `customerId` and a per-customer Map keyed by product ID.
Expose synchronous `saveWishlistItem`, `getWishlist` and `removeWishlistItem` operations and their types through `src/index.ts`.
Store only product IDs and first-save timestamps; use the existing catalogue lookup to validate saves and resolve current details on reads.
Preserve duplicate saves, sort reads newest first and keep every operation within the addressed customer's wishlist.
Use `bun:test` claim coverage with explicit dates and distinct customers; retain the [model sketch](reference/data-model.md) and [contract draft](reference/module-design.md) as working material.

## Trade-offs

Sanne chose process-local storage and exported module operations over persistence or a UI, as recorded in the [accepted decision](../../decisions/2026-10-13-wishlist-module-and-storage.md). This keeps the existing setup and loses wishlist state on restart.

## Files

```text
src/
  wishlist.ts      new: store, types and save/view/remove operations
  index.ts         changed: re-export wishlist functions and types
test/
  wishlist.test.ts new: claim coverage and public export verification
```

## Architecture to update at ship

- `docs/architecture/data-model.md`, from [reference/data-model.md](reference/data-model.md).
- `docs/architecture/boundaries.md`, from [reference/module-design.md](reference/module-design.md).
- `docs/architecture/contracts.md`, from [reference/module-design.md](reference/module-design.md).
- `docs/architecture/stack.md`, from [reference/module-design.md](reference/module-design.md).

## Risks

- A repeated save could replace the original time or move an item; `preserve-first-save` and `newest-first` prove the ordering.
- Shared module state could mix customers; `isolate-wishlists` and `isolate-removal` prove separation, with distinct test customers preventing fixture overlap.
- Stored product snapshots could return old prices; `current-product-details` proves that reads use the current catalogue.

Purpose: retain the wishlist data model sketch as working material for implementation and the architecture update at ship.

# Wishlist data model sketch

This is the proposed model for this spec, not a description of shipped code.

| Value | Proposed fields or shape | Relations |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Module-local wishlist store | `Map<string, Map<string, WishlistItem>>` | The outer key is the supplied `customerId`; the inner key is `productId`, allowing one entry per product per customer. |
| `WishlistItem` | `productId: string`, `savedAt: Date` | References a catalogue product by ID; stores its first save moment without quantity, name or price snapshots. |
| `WishlistProduct` | `productId: string`, `name: string`, `priceCents: number`, `savedAt: Date` | A read projection combining a saved entry with current details from the existing catalogue in `src/products.ts`. |

## Storage and reads

- Create a customer's inner Map only after a catalogue product has been resolved successfully for the first save.
- Copy the supplied save time on insertion. A repeated save returns the existing entry's values without changing its timestamp or position.
- Resolve names and prices from the catalogue for each read, then order entries by descending `savedAt`. Equal timestamps retain insertion order.
- Return fresh item values and copied dates so callers cannot mutate the stored entries through returned values or the supplied clock value.
- Removing an entry addresses only the supplied customer's Map; an empty customer Map can be discarded.
- An absent customer Map reads as an empty list. There is no separate customer record or wishlist ID.

## Scope of the sketch

The spec leaves disappearing catalogue products and stock handling outside this change; this draft adds no behavior for those cases.
Catalogue field access must use the existing exports and types when implementation begins; the catalogue itself is outside the change scope.
Keep this file as working material after shipping; update `docs/architecture/data-model.md` from the implemented model instead of moving this draft there.
Purpose: draft the wishlist contracts, module boundary and verification approach that inform implementation and architecture updates at ship.

# Wishlist module draft

## Public contracts

| Export | Proposed contract | Result and errors |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `saveWishlistItem` | `(customerId: string, productId: string, now?: Date): WishlistItem` | Validate catalogue membership and save a product; default `now` to the current time. Return a copy of the new or existing saved entry. Throw `Error` for an unknown product. |
| `getWishlist` | `(customerId: string): WishlistProduct[]` | Return the customer's saved products with current names and prices in newest-first order; return an empty list for a customer with no entries. |
| `removeWishlistItem` | `(customerId: string, productId: string): void` | Remove the addressed customer's saved entry; throw `Error` if the entry is absent, including when that customer has no wishlist. |
| `WishlistItem` | Exported TypeScript type | The stored product ID and first save time described in [the model sketch](data-model.md). |
| `WishlistProduct` | Exported TypeScript type | The read projection described in [the model sketch](data-model.md). |

Customer IDs are used as supplied; do not add customer lookup, sign-in or normalization.
The draft does not promise exact error message text.

## Module boundary

- Implement the store, types and synchronous operations in `src/wishlist.ts`, using the existing catalogue lookup from `src/products.ts` and JavaScript built-ins.
- Re-export the public functions and types through `src/index.ts` using that file's existing export convention.
- Put the claim tests in `test/wishlist.test.ts`. The store remains private; tests use distinct customer IDs rather than adding a public reset API.
- Use the existing TypeScript and Bun setup. No new packages, configuration, database, UI or changes to the catalogue module are planned.

## Verification design

- Name behavioral tests with full references such as `wishlist/save-items#save-item`; cover all 12 claims in the approved spec.
- Use explicit dates for duplicate-save and ordering examples, without sleeps. Exercise save/read sequences to prove that successful saves actually remain in the customer's wishlist.
- For `current-product-details`, arrange for a catalogue price to change between save and read using the existing catalogue test facilities, and restore any changed fixture or mock afterward. Do not add a production catalogue mutation API for this test.
- Exercise two customers independently for reads and removal, including a failed removal from a customer without the saved product.
- Verify the three functions through `src/index.ts` after adding the barrel exports, and run the complete `bun test` suite for regressions.

## Architecture sources at ship

- `docs/architecture/boundaries.md`: the Wishlist module, its source and test paths, catalogue dependency and public barrel.
- `docs/architecture/contracts.md`: the implemented public contracts listed above.
- `docs/architecture/stack.md`: the expanded TypeScript and Bun usage; retain the existing `bun test` command.

Keep this draft as working material after shipping; architecture records the verified implementation.

# Keep wishlists in an in-memory module

## Context

The wishlist needs state associated with a caller-supplied customer ID and operations for saving, viewing and removing products.
Sanne chose in-memory storage keyed by customer ID and a module-only implementation in this planning session.
The approved spec introduces neither sign-in nor a customer entity.

## Options

- A module-local Map keyed by customer ID: chosen by Sanne to keep storage in memory like the other modules.
- Persistent storage: would retain wishlists across restarts but introduce storage infrastructure outside the chosen scope.
- Exported TypeScript operations: chosen by Sanne for this repository's integration surface.
- A UI: would introduce a presentation surface outside the chosen scope.

## Decision

Implement wishlists in `src/wishlist.ts` with a module-local Map keyed by `customerId`, tests in `test/wishlist.test.ts` and exports from `src/index.ts`.

## Consequences

The feature can use the existing TypeScript and Bun setup without a database or UI.
Wishlists disappear on process restart and are independent in separate processes.
The supplied customer ID selects a wishlist; this module does not establish a caller's identity.
A future persistence or presentation change needs a new decision and its own spec.
